definitions.explanation: A heavily fortified military structure or position designed for defense. Used both for historical castles and fortifications and in modern figurative contexts for impregnable places.

examples.japanese: {敵|てき}の{要塞|ようさい}を{攻|せ}める。
この{島|しま}はかつて{軍事|ぐんじ}{要塞|ようさい}として{使|つか}われていた。
examples.english: This island was once used as a military fortress.

examples.japanese: {難攻不落|なんこうふらく}の{要塞|ようさい}がついに{陥落|かんらく}した。

notes:
USAGE:
{要塞|ようさい} refers specifically to fortified military positions, as opposed to {城|しろ} (castle), which may serve as a residence. {要塞|ようさい} emphasizes the defensive, strategic nature of the structure. The word appears frequently in historical, military, and gaming contexts. It can also be used figuratively to describe any extremely well-protected place.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {要塞|ようさい}を{築|きず}く: to build a fortress
- {要塞|ようさい}を{攻略|こうりゃく}する: to conquer a fortress
- {軍事|ぐんじ}{要塞|ようさい}: military fortress
- {難攻不落|なんこうふらく}の{要塞|ようさい}: impregnable fortress
